newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, Korean buyers cheer tumble in wheat prices.
newsitem.headline: Japan, Korean buyers cheer tumble in wheat prices.

text.p: Tumbling wheat prices in the U.S. have brought cheer to Japanese and South Korean buyers, with prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) expected to slide further in the coming weeks, traders said on Tuesday.
"Cheaper prices are good news for us importers, of course," Shinichi Yahagi, director of the Japan Food Agency's trade division, told Reuters.
The Food Agency, one of the world's largest grain buyers, is Japan's sole importer of wheat, barley and rice. It issues an import tender every Thursday.
Japanese trade houses say they expect Chicago wheat futures prices to fall further due to soft demand in the market.
"We expect the July contract of Chicago wheat market to fall further to US$3.00 (a bushel) levels, considering a lack of strong demand," a wheat dealer at a trade house in Japan said.
A trader with Cheil Futures in Korea pegged short-term support for wheat futures on the CBOT also at $3.00 a bushel.
"The next support (will) be at $2.80," he added.

Wheat prices on the CBOT slid to a fresh three-year low on Monday with July dropping to a contract low of $3.13 a bushel before ending 6-3/4 U.S. cents down at $3.13-1/2. The previous low was set last week at $3.19-1/2 a bushel.
September was down 5-3/4 cents at $3.21-3/4.

In the CBOT's Project A after-hours trading system in Asia, the July wheat contract equalled the low of $3.13 a bushel at 0816 GMT while the September contract slipped to a session low of $3.21 a bushel.
Traders said falling wheat prices would lure South Korean flour milling companies to cover their needs for forward delivery this week.

Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd bought 21,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat on Tuesday from Japanese trading house Mitsubishi Corp. The wheat is for September 5 to October 5 shipment to the western port of Inchon.
Daehan said it would buy an additional 21,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat this week for September 20 to October 20 shipment.

Traders said Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd were also expected to jointly tender for 21,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat for shipment between September 5 to October 5, or between Setember 1-30 to the southeastern port of Pusan.
Korea Flour Milling Corp was expected to buy about 17,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat this week for shipment in September.
Korean feed millers were also mulling buying some 52,500 tonnes of U.S. corn at a tender later on Tuesday.
Yahagi said the pace of Japanese buying remained unaffected by the sharp fall in prices on the CBOT.
"We've been buying wheat and barley (at a) constant pace, and recent price falls (in the) wheat market will not accelerate our buying," he said.
Yahagi said offer prices of Australian wheat were likewise falling gradually, in line with the slide on the Chicago market.

The Food Agency postponed buying of some Australian grain last month because offer prices were too high and Yahagi said at that time the Food Agency may cancel some imports if the Australian Wheat Board failed to lower prices.
"But (the) Australian side is now adjusting offer prices in line with the Chicago market," Yahagi said.
